mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods with sustained RSAFS growth, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the joint effect of HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL growth < 1%) coupled with low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) suggests a supportive monetary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth < 1% and FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 months
regime_hint: low inflation and accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the joint effect of low CPIAUCSL growth and low FEDFUNDS on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods with sustained PAYEMS growth, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals a significant economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to fall.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
